36 A computer is used to detect the change of position of a switch.
To detect the change of position, the computer requires a potential difference (p.d.) of 0 V to its
input at one switch position and a p.d. of between 5 V and 7 V at the other switch position.
For each of the circuits, assume the battery has negligible internal resistance.
Which circuit provides an input voltage to the computer that enables it to detect the change of
position of the switch?

hints: Look at where the switch is placed in A and B compared with C and D, and decide what the computer input voltage is when the switch is open and no current flows.
For the closed-switch position use the potential divider rule for the voltage across the lower resistor: $V_{out} = 9\text{ V} \times R_{lower}/(R_{upper}+R_{lower})$.
Check each closed-switch result against the required $5\text{ V}$ to $7\text{ V}$ window while also requiring exactly $0\text{ V}$ in the open-switch position.
walkthrough: Identify the two states: switch open means the series loop is broken so current $I = 0$, while switch closed means a $9\text{ V}$ potential divider is connected.
In A and B the computer input is across the lower resistor with its bottom lead to the battery negative. When open, $I=0$ so there is no p.d. across either resistor and the input is $0\text{ V}$.

When closed, apply $V_{input} = 9\text{ V} \times R_{lower}/(R_{upper}+R_{lower})$. For the $1\text{ k}\Omega$ upper and $2\text{ k}\Omega$ lower circuit, $V_{input} = 9 \times 2/(1+2) = 6.0\text{ V}$.
Check the requirement: $0\text{ V}$ in one position and between $5\text{ V}$ and $7\text{ V}$ in the other. $0\text{ V}$ and $6.0\text{ V}$ satisfies both with correct units of $\text{V}$.
Circuits C and D fail because with the switch open the top resistor connects the upper input lead to $9\text{ V}$ with no voltage drop, giving $9\text{ V}$ not $0\text{ V}$. This is option B

A.explanation: With the switch closed the $1\text{ k}\Omega$ - $1\text{ k}\Omega$ divider gives $9 \times 1/(1+1) = 4.5\text{ V}$, which is below the required $5\text{ V}$ to $7\text{ V}$ range.

B.explanation: With the switch open the input is $0\text{ V}$ and with it closed the $1\text{ k}\Omega$ - $2\text{ k}\Omega$ divider gives $6\text{ V}$, which meets the $0\text{ V}$ and $5\text{ V}$ to $7\text{ V}$ requirement.

C.explanation: With the switch open there is no current so the middle point stays at $9\text{ V}$ to the lower terminal, and closed it falls to about $1.8\text{ V}$, so $0\text{ V}$ is never obtained.

D.explanation: With the switch open the input is $9\text{ V}$ because the $500\,\Omega$ resistor has no current, and closed it is about $7.2\text{ V}$, so $0\text{ V}$ is never obtained.
